name: CommandPaletteButton
summary: Search-styled trigger that opens the global command palette. Carries leading search icon, placeholder hint, and trailing keyboard-shortcut chip.

hint.description: Placeholder-style hint, rendered in muted text.

shortcutKey.description: Keyboard letter for the shortcut. Default 'K' — paired with platform modifier (⌘ on Mac, Ctrl elsewhere).

onClick.description: Open the actual palette. The component is just the trigger.

keyboard: Tab - move focus to next control
{platform-modifier}+{shortcutKey} - global shortcut to open the palette
rules: Implement the global keyboard shortcut at the app level (window event listener) — the trigger is just the visible affordance.
The platform modifier auto-detects on the client; SSR renders 'Ctrl' as the safe default.
kbd chip must use mono typography (Lumen type.kbd).
If the palette is the primary nav for power users, place the trigger high in the visual hierarchy (top-bar centre or right-of-logo).

do: Pair with the global keyboard shortcut. Without the shortcut the trigger is just a button.
Use a verb-noun hint: 'Find a lane, load, customer' — concrete examples beat 'Search'.
Place at top-bar centre or right of logo, the universal place power users look.
dont: Don't use CommandPaletteButton as a substitute for a real search input — the palette is for navigation + quick actions, not field-search.
Don't omit the kbd chip — operators rely on the visual hint to discover the shortcut.

changelog.note: Formal CommandPaletteButton primitive. Search-styled outline button + leading Search icon + trailing platform-aware kbd chip.
